chunks: A group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from his brother Al-Hasan, from Zurara, from Sama'ah, who said:
I asked him about laughing, does it break the prayer? He said: As for smiling, it does not break the prayer, and as for chuckling (laughing aloud), it breaks the prayer.
ai.seo_question: Does laughing break the prayer in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the jurisprudential boundary between minor amusement and significant distraction during prayer, a distinction crucial for maintaining the khushu (focus) required in Shia fiqh. By contrasting 'tabassum' (a subtle smile) with 'qahqaha' (audible, deep laughter), the narrator Samaanah clarifies that only laughter of a magnitude that breaks concentration invalidates the salāt, reflecting the scholarly emphasis on the internal state of the worshipper.

en.hubeali: A group, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from his brother Al Hassan, from Zurara, from Sama’at who said,
‘I asked about the one who laughs, would it cut the Salāt?’ Heasws said: ‘As for the smile, so it does not cut off the Salāt, and as for the chuckling (laughing), so it cuts off the Salāt’.
en.sarwar: 1. A group has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from his brother al-Hassan, from Zur’ah, from Sama‘ah who has said the following:

“I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about laughing if it destroys Salah (prayer). He (the Imam) said, ‘Smiling does not destroy Salah (prayer) but laughing loudly destroys it.’” It (the above Hadith) also is narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah.”
